title: Open-Loop PID Autotuner
text: Automatically tune PID gains based on plant frequency responses estimated from open-loop experiment in real time, 7 inputs, 7 outputs, {Type} sets PID controller actions PI; {Form} sets the pID controller form, {Time Domain} sets the pID controller time, {Controller sample time (sec)} sets the sample time of PID controller, {Experiment sample time (sec)} sets the sample time for experiment, {Integrator method} sets the discrete integration formula for integrator term Forward, {Filter method} sets the discrete integration formula for derivative filter term Forward, {Target bandwidth (rad/sec)} sets the target crossover frequency of tuned, {Target phase margin (degrees)} sets the target minimum phase margin of open-loop, {Sine Amplitudes} sets the amplitude of sinusoidal perturbations, {Estimate DC gain with step signal} sets the inject step signal into plant, {Step Amplitude} sets the amplitude of step perturbation, {Reduce memory and avoid task overrun (external mode only)} sets the deploy tuning algorithm only, {Configure block for PLC Coder} sets the configure block for code generation with Simulink PLC, {Data Type} sets the floating point precision, {Clicking "Update PID Block" writes tuned gains to the PID block connected to "u" port} sets the automatically detect target for writing tuned PID, {Specify PID block path} sets the target PID controller block for writing tuned coefficients, {Update PID Block} sets the write tuned PID gains to target controller block and {Export to MATLAB} sets the send experiment and tuning results to MATLAB workspace. Values come from the instance.
